On-Chain Operator. Lesson 14.1, Monitoring: dashboards, alerts and on-chain watchers. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already have a playbook. Automation may watch it. Automation may not hold your keys.
Positions: health factors, LP ranges, pegs, utilisation of markets you lend to.
Wallets: any outgoing transaction or new approval from your vault/operating wallets.
Tools: portfolio dashboards, protocol-native alerts, wallet-activity watchers, block-explorer address alerts, and official status/X accounts.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Alerts for all four categories, delivered to phone. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Every alert maps to a written action. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Why alert on any vault-wallet outflow? The answer: The vault should almost never move; any movement could be a compromise.
Check yourself. 2. Why watch queued upgrades? The answer: The timelock is your window to exit before the change takes effect.
Check yourself. 3. An alert with no action attached is…? The answer: Noise. Every alert needs a written response.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to set up monitoring so you hear about problems before they cost money.
